rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusrā denotes good deeds that lead to ease.
rows.anchor: اليسرى هي أعمال الخير التي تؤدي إلى اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with 87:6, with the knowledge clause parenthetical; God enables the easiest path, especially memorizing the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ونوفقك للطريقة التي هي أسهل وأيسر ، يعني في حفظ القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-yusrā means Paradise, and God enables the Prophet to do the deeds that lead to it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : اليسرى الجنة ، والمعنى نيسرك للعمل المؤدى إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God makes revelation easy for the Prophet to memorize, understand, and act upon.
rows.anchor: نهون عليك الوحي حتى تحفظه وتعلمه وتعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God guides the Prophet to the easy, tolerant hanifī law.
rows.anchor: نوفقك للشريعة وهي الحنيفية السهلة السمحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording makes the agent enabled for an act: a merely possible act occurs only when doing outweighs refraining, and that preponderance is facilitation; the Prophet’s hadith uses the same wording.
rows.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له ) وفيه لطيفة علمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic plural magnifies the gift by magnifying its giver, as in other divine first-person plurals.
rows.anchor: إنما قال : { ونيسرك لليسرى } بنون التعظيم لتكون عظمة المعطى دالة على عظمة العطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God opened exceptional paths of ease for Muhammad: an orphan raised among an ignorant people became a model in words and deeds for all creation.
rows.anchor: فتح عليه من أبواب التيسير والستهيل ما لم يفتحه على أحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Muhammad unmatched facilitation and made him, despite his orphaned upbringing among an ignorant people, a universal exemplar.
rows.anchor: كان صبيا لا أب له ولا أم له نشأ في قوم جهال ، ثم إنه تعالى جعله في أفعاله وأقواله قدوة للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the Prophet through ease, God commands reminder to bring deficient people to completion and guide the ignorant, making him an emanator of perfection.
rows.anchor: لأن التذكير يقتضي تكميل الناقصين وهداية الجاهلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conditional clause does not entail that the action ceases when its condition is absent; Qur’anic examples include the captive women, gratitude, travel prayer, pledges, and reconciliation.
rows.anchor: أن المعلق بأن على الشيء لا يلزم أن يكون عدما عند عدم ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rationale is that an act pursued as a means to an end is more compelling when it is known to achieve that end.
rows.anchor: الصورة التي علم فيها إفضاء تلك الوسيلة إلى ذلك الغرض ، كان إلى ذلك الفعل أوجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second rationale names the most favorable case while alluding to the alternative: remind whether or not the reminder benefits.
rows.anchor: ذكر أشرف الحالتين ، ونبه على الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third rationale uses the condition to urge acceptance and benefit, like telling someone that the truth was clarified if they understand.
rows.anchor: المراد منه البعث على الانتفاع بالذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth rationale hints that the audience is unlikely to answer, as when one says to invite someone if he responds.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أن هذا يجري مجرى تنبيه الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth rationale consoles the Prophet: repeated calls increased their defiance and his grief, while repetition may be required only when success is hoped for; the initial general call remains obligatory.
rows.anchor: إذ التذكير العام واجب في أول الأمر فأما التكرير فلعله إنما يجب عند رجاء حصول المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call people and God’s knowledge of the unseen are distinct; the command is not grounded in uncertainty about the outcome.
rows.anchor: فأمر الدعوة والبعثة شيء وعلمه تعالى بالمغيبات وعواقب الأمور غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has God tell Moses to speak gently to Pharaoh while affirming that Pharaoh will not remember or fear.
rows.anchor: روي في الكتب أنه تعالى كان يقول لموسى : { فقولا له قولا لينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty’s repetition has no fixed count; custom supplies the measure.
rows.anchor: أن الضابط فيه هو العرف والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fall into those certain of resurrection, those who suspend judgment, and deniers; the first two groups fear, while deniers do not.
rows.anchor: القسمان الأولان تكون الخشية حاصلة لهما ، وأما القسم الثالث فلا خشية له ولا خوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading identifies the fearful as those who know God’s power, knowledge, and wisdom and therefore are certain of resurrection; 35:28 links fear to scholars.
rows.anchor: الذي يخشى هو الذي يكون عارفا بالله وعارفا بكمال قدرته وعلمه وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because inward fear is hidden from the Messenger, he must address everyone to reach those who will benefit from reminder.
rows.anchor: صفات القلوب مما لا اطلاع لأحد عليها إلا الله سبحانه وجب على الرسول تعميم الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, most people are hesitant rather than defiant, many opponents resist only outwardly, and warnings of Hell break their hearts; thus general reminder benefits most.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الخلق متوقفون غير معاندين والمعاند فيهم قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future tense may promise certain remembrance, since God’s future acts are assured, or describe fearful people remembering later through reflection.
rows.anchor: السين في قوله : { سيذكر } يحتمل أن تكون بمعنى سوف يذكر وسوف من الله واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers’ recollection is called remembrance because the proofs are so clear that their knowledge seems already present, then removed by imitation and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: لقوة الدلائل وظهورها كأن ذلك العلم كان حاصلا ، ثم إنه زال بسبب التقليد والعناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت هذه الآية في عثمان بن عفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says it was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of the knowing, hesitant, and defiant groups, the most wretched is the obstinate person who ignores the call and gains no benefit from it.
rows.anchor: الأشقى هو المعاند الذي لا يستمع إلى الدعوة ولا ينتفع بها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The greater fire is Hell, in contrast with the lesser fire of this world.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : الكبرى نار جهنم ، والصغرى نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the afterlife contains fires and levels of differing severity, and the worst sinner enters the greatest fire.
rows.anchor: أن في الآخرة نيرانا ودركات متفاضلة كماأن في الدنيا ذنوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation makes the greater fire the lowest level, where disbelievers are placed, as 4:145 says of hypocrites.
rows.anchor: النار الكبرى هي النار السفلى ، وهي تصيب الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports tie the revelation to al-Walid, Utba, and Abi, but the wording applies generally and the sequence is also rationally established.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الوليد وعتبة وأبي ، وأنت تعلم أن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative does not require a separate class of merely wretched people; Arabic can use it without comparison, as 25:24 does.
rows.anchor: لفظة الأشقى لا تقتضي وجود الشقي إذ قد يجري مثل هذا اللفظ من غير مشاركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construes the word as the wretched one, like 30:27 meaning easy; an Arabic poetic line is also cited for this usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ، ويتجنبها الشقي الذي يصلى كما في قوله : { وهو أهون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound account keeps three classes: the knower is felicitous, the hesitant has some misery, and the obstinate who spurns the call is most wretched.
rows.anchor: السعيد هو العارف ، والمتوقف له بعض الشقاء والأشقى هو المعاند

none: Verse heading only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the damned neither die to find relief nor live a life of benefit; Arabs use this idiom for extreme suffering, as 35:36 does.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the soul reaches the throat but cannot leave in death or return to the body in life.
rows.anchor: نفس أحدهم في النار تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج فيموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks a further stage because this state is more terrible than entering the fire and is delayed in the progression of severity.
rows.anchor: هذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه في مراتب الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself from the previously mentioned disbelief, since the verse does not name another object of purification.
rows.anchor: لما لم يذكر في الآية ما يجب التزكي عنه علمنا أن المراد هو التزكي عما مر ذكره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, purification means increasing in piety, since zakā carries the sense of growth; 23:1–2 and 2:5 associate success with gathered virtues.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج : تكثر من التقوى لأن معنى الزاكي النامي الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted word refers to its fullest sense: purifying the heart from disbelief’s darkness is the highest purification.
rows.anchor: الاسم المطلق ينصرف إلى المسمى الكامل ، وأكمل أنواع التزكية هو تزكية القلب عن ظلمة الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses purification as declaring that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: بما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معنى : { تزكى } قول : لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembering God’s name means recalling resurrection and standing before Him, then praying; al-Razi deems this interpretation determinate.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه فصلى له . وأقول : هذا التفسير متعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence describes three stages: removing false beliefs, knowing God through His names and attributes, then serving Him through humble prayer.
rows.anchor: فالمرتبة الأولى : هي المراد بالتزكية في قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى

rows.speaker: عكرمة، أبو العالية، ابن سيرين، ابن عمر
rows.claim: A group interprets the passage as charity before Eid followed by Eid prayer; this is also reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول عكرمة وأبي العالية وابن سيرين وابن عمر وروي ذلك مرفوعا إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That Eid interpretation faces the Qur’an’s usual order of prayer before alms and the sura’s Meccan setting, where neither Eid nor fitra existed.
rows.anchor: أن عادة الله تعالى في القرآن تقديم ذكر الصلاة على ذكر الزكاة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi answers that God may praise people in advance for practices He knows will occur later.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يقال : لما كان في معلوم الله تعالى أن ذلك سيكون أثنى على من فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reads the first phrase as giving alms and the second as affirming oneness in prayer; unlike the Eid view, this concerns obligatory alms and prayer.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ( الأعلى : 14 ) أي تصدق من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes purification as cleansing deeds of ostentation and shortcomings, not paying wealth-alms; the wording fits deeds, as 35:18 says.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد منه زكاة المال بل زكاة الأعمال أي من تطهر في أعماله من الرياء والتقصير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further report says the worshipper proclaims God’s greatness while going out to Eid, then performs the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { وذكر اسم ربه } أي كبر في خروجه إلى العيد وصلى صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is remembrance within prayer, unlike hypocrites who perform for show and remember God only a little.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه في صلاته ولا تكون صلاته كصلاة المنافقين حيث يراؤون الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists cite this verse as evidence that the opening takbīr is obligatory.
rows.anchor: الفقهاء احتجوا بهذه الآية على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that opening takbīr is outside prayer because coordination marks distinct things, and that any divine name may open prayer.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بها على أن تكبيرة الافتتاح ليست من الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response notes that the implied order could be pray and then remember, since reversing the order of clauses can preserve the sense.
rows.anchor: تقدير الآية ، وصلى فذكر اسم ربه ولا فرق بين أن تقول أكرمتني فزرتني

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa objects that the sequential force of the fāʾ cannot be set aside without evidence.
rows.anchor: ترك العمل بفاء التعقيب لا يجوز من غير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse praises anyone who remembers God and then prays but never identifies that remembrance as the opening takbīr; reflection on reward and punishment may instead prompt prayer.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على مدح كل من ذكر اسم الله فصلى عقيبه وليس في الآية بيان أن ذلك الذكر هو تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading uses second-person plural, reinforced by Ubayy’s wording: you prefer worldly work to afterlife work.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة بالتاء ويؤكده حرف أبي ، أي بل أنتم تؤثرون عمل الدنيا على عمل الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud explains that worldly food, drink, women, and pleasures are immediate and visible, while the afterlife is unseen, so people choose the near reward.
rows.anchor: إن الدنيا أحضرت ، وعجل لنا طعامها وشرابها ونساؤها ولذاتها وبهجتها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads in the third person, referring to the most wretched as those who prefer worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : يؤثرون بالياء يعني الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever is better and more enduring is more deserving of preference, so the afterlife ought to be preferred over the worldly life people choose.
rows.anchor: كل ما كان خيرا وأبقى فهو آثر ، فيلزم أن تكون الآخرة آثر من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife surpasses this world because it combines bodily and spiritual happiness.
rows.anchor: الآخرة مشتملة على السعادة الجسمانية والروحانية ، والدنيا ليست كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures are mixed with pains, whereas afterlife pleasures are not.
rows.anchor: أن الدنيا لذاتها مخلوطة بالآلام ، والآخرة ليست كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife lasts while worldly life passes away; permanence is better than transience.
rows.anchor: أن الدنيا فانية ، والآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من الفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes this as the whole sura, which includes divine oneness, prophecy, a warning against disbelief, and a promise for obedience.
rows.anchor: جميع السورة ، وذلك لأن السورة مشتملة على التوحيد والنبوة والوعيد على الكفر بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view reads 87:14–17 as a sequence: purify intellect and morals, complete the spirit through knowledge of God, complete the limbs through obedience, reject worldly attachment, and seek the afterlife; these truths cross religious laws.
rows.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى تكميل الروح بمعرفة الله تعالى ، وأما قوله : { فصلى }

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr asks whether the teachings occur in Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls; the Prophet tells him to read 87:14.
rows.anchor: روى عن أبي ذر أنه قال : قلت هل في الدنيا مما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟ فقال : اقرأ يا أبا ذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view points only to the nearest antecedent, 87:17, and compares the reference to 26:196 and 42:13.
rows.anchor: إن قوله هذا إشارة إلى قوله : { والاخرة خير وأبقى } وذلك لأن الإشارة راجعة إلى أقرب المذكورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words identify which earlier scriptures are meant by the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه بيان لقوله : { فى الصحف الاولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the teaching appears in the scriptures of all prophets; a report from Abu Dharr lists 104 revealed books, including the ten given to Abraham.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying attributed to Abraham’s scrolls advises the wise to guard the tongue, know the age, and attend to one’s own affairs.
rows.anchor: في صحف إبراهيم : ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ghashiya chapter is Meccan and has twenty-six verses.
rows.anchor: وهي عشرون وست آيات مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghāshiya is most plausibly the Resurrection: it overtakes people suddenly, encompasses everyone, and envelops them in terrors.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنها القيامة من قوله : { يوم يغشاهم العذاب }

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، مقاتل
rows.claim: Another view identifies al-Ghāshiya as Hell, which covers the faces of its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view takes al-Ghāshiya to mean the people who cover the fire by entering it.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : الغاشية أهل النار يغشونها ويقعون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether the Prophet has heard the report introduces revealed details unavailable to reason, which can establish only the general difference between sinners and the obedient.
rows.anchor: لأن العقل إن دل فإنه لا يدل إلا على أن حال العصاة مخالفة لحال المطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces stands for their owners, the accountable disbelievers, since humility and effort are qualities of persons; humiliation shows on faces, as in 75:22, 32:12, and 42:45.
rows.anchor: المراد بالوجوه أصحاب الوجوه وهم الكفار ، بدليل أنه تعالى وصف الوجوه بأنها خاشعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashiʿa means abased by disgrace; abasement appears in the face as the opposite of pride, whose seat is the head and brain.
rows.anchor: وإنما يظهر الذل في الوجه ، لأنه ضد الكبر الذي محله الرأس والدماغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are working with exertion, and nāṣiba describes persistent labor accompanied by fatigue.
rows.anchor: ومعنى النصب الدؤوب في العمل مع التعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three attributes may all describe the afterlife: humbled after worldly pride, the damned labor by dragging chains, struggling through fire, or enduring the naked, hungry, thirsty court before Hell, and remain in toil; Hasan says their worldly failure merits this punishment.
rows.anchor: يكونون يوم القيامة خاشعين أي ذليلين ، وذلك لأنها في الدنيا تكبرت عن عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all three describe worldly life, they may refer to Jewish and Christian monks, idolaters, and Magians who fast and pray intensely, yet worship an imagined deity because their beliefs misdescribe God; their worship therefore does not benefit them.
rows.anchor: هم أصحاب الصوامع من اليهود والنصارى وعبدة الأوثان والمجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mixed reading places humiliation in the afterlife but futile work and toil in worldly life, followed by the fiery punishment.
rows.anchor: أنها خاشعة في الآخرة ، مع أنها كانت في الدنيا عاملة ناصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another mixed reading places fear and worship in worldly life and toil in the afterlife: fear turns people from pleasure, their work is prayer and fasting, and their later toil is punishment, as 39:47 indicates.
rows.anchor: خشوعها في الدنيا خوفها الداعي لها إلى الإعراض عن لذائذ الدنيا وطيباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading gives āmila nāṣiba a use of insult or blame.
rows.anchor: وقرىء عاملة ناصبة على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing these people, God proceeds to explain their place, drink, and food.
rows.anchor: شرح بعد ذلك كيفية مكانهم ومشربهم ومطعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their abode is a fiercely hot fire.
rows.anchor: أما مكانهم فقوله تعالى : { تصلى نارا حامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ṣaliya means to remain by a fire and burn in it.
rows.anchor: يقال : صلى بالنار يصلى أي لزمها واحترق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading puts the tāʾ in the accusative, supported by the description of one who is destined to burn in Hell in 37:163.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بنصب التاء وحجته قوله : { إلا من هو صال الجحيم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو، عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Asim read the tāʾ in the nominative, with the fire as the agent; the wording is supported by 69:31 and the form وصلوه.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم برفع التاء من أصيلته النار لقوله : { ثم الجحيم صلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers pronounce the verb with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم تصلى بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arab usage, a musallā is a pit filled with embers into which a sheep is placed; roasting above embers, on a pan, or in an oven is not called that.
rows.anchor: أن يحفروا حفيرا فيجمعوا فيه جمرا كثيرا ، ثم يعمدوا إلى شاة فيدسوها وسطه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ḥāmia means heated after a long period of burning; no heat can match it, and it blazes against God’s enemies.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : قد حميت فهي تتلظى على أعداء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āni describes water whose heat has reached its limit; the word derives from īnā, meaning delay.
rows.anchor: الآني الذي قد انتهى حره من الإيناء بمعنى التأخير

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet rebuked a man who arrived late to Friday prayer and pushed through people, saying he was late and caused harm.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : آنيت وآذيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase parallels 55:44; exegetes say a drop of the water’s heat would melt the world’s mountains.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : إن حرها بلغ إلى حيث لو وقعت منها قطرة على جبال الدنيا لذابت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says he does not know what al-ḍarīʿ is and has heard nothing about it from the Companions.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : لا أدري ما الضريع ولم أسمع فيه من الصحابة شيئا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan also explains it as something that makes its eater supplicate and abase himself because of its roughness, bitterness, and heat.
rows.anchor: روى عن الحسن أيضا أنه قال : الضريع بمعنى المضرع كالأليم والسميع

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأكثر أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Most exegetes and linguists identify it as dried shibriq, a thorn camels eat fresh but avoid when dry; it is lethal poison. Abu Dhuʾayb’s verse attests the word’s meaning.
rows.anchor: أن الضريع ما يبس من الشبرق ، وهو جنس من الشوك ترعاه الإبل ما دام رطبا

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s line uses ḍarīʿ for the dried thorn that camels avoid.
rows.anchor: رعى الشبرق الريان حتى إذا ذوى … وعاد ضريعا عاد عنه النحائص

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says ḍarīʿ is the membrane on a bone beneath its meat, suggesting a scant food that cannot nourish.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل في كتابه : ويقال للجلدة التي على العظم تحت اللحم هي الضريع

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Jawzaʾ identifies it as spleen; Saʿid ibn Jubayr describes a thorn tree, and an unspecified report calls it a thornlike substance in Hell, bitterer than colocynth, fouler than carrion, and hotter than fire.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الجوزاء : الضريع السلا ، ويقرب منه ما روي عن سعيد بن جبير أنه شجرة ذات شوك

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the water and plant intensify humiliation: after prolonged thirst and hunger, the water burns and the plant neither satiates nor relieves them, ending hope; 18:29 offers a parallel.
rows.anchor: فأحب أولئك القوم تسكين ما بهم من العطش والجوع فوجدوا الماء حميما لا يروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different foods in 69:35–36 need not conflict: Hell has levels with different provisions, or ghislin may be a kind of ḍarīʿ just as milk comes from sheep.
rows.anchor: من أهل النار من طعامه الزقوم ، ومنهم من طعامه الغسلين ، ومنهم من طعامه الضريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to how a plant grows in Hell is that ḍarīʿ is figurative: the damned eat what does not satisfy or suffer hunger like someone fed thorns.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد أن الضريع نبت في النار يأكلونه ، ولكنه ضرب مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a plant may exist in Hell just as human bodies persist there; the same applies to chains, scorpions, and snakes.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال : إن النبت يوجد في النار ؟ فإنه لما لم يستبعد بقاء بدن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can be parsed as nominative or genitive, describing either the food or the ḍarīʿ.
rows.anchor: فهو مرفوع المحل أو مجروره على وصف طعام أو ضريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning is that this thorn is not food for humans: camels shun it, so it supplies neither relief from hunger nor bodily strength and fat.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع مما ينفر عنه الإبل ، فإذن منفعتا الغذاء منتفيتان عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning denies that they have food at all, since food by definition nourishes and satisfies; the phrase resembles saying there is no shade except the sun.
rows.anchor: أن الضريع ليس بطعام للبهائم فضلا عن الإنس لأن الطعام ما أشبع وأسمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh claimed ḍarīʿ fattens camels: either they lied, or Hell’s thorn is unlike the earthly plant they knew.
rows.anchor: روي أن كفار قريش قالت : إن الضريع لتسمن عليه إبلنا

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Judge argues that none of their food can relieve hunger, since such benefit and mercy are incompatible with punishment.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : يجب في كل طعامهم أن لا يغني من جوع لأن ذلك نفع ورأفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the disbelievers’ warning, God describes the reward’s people and their abode, beginning with the people themselves.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر وعيد الكفار ، أتبعه بشرح أحوال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faces are radiant and beautiful, as 83:24 says, or they are at ease and enjoying blessing.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله : { ناعمة } أي ذات بهجة وحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says they approve their own efforts because the good outcome shows that they worked well.
rows.anchor: حمدوا سعيهم واجتهادهم في العمل لله . لما فازوا بسببه من العاقبة الحميدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better reading is that they are pleased with the reward for their worldly striving, which satisfies them so fully they want nothing more.
rows.anchor: المراد لثواب سعيها في الدنيا راضية إذا شاهدوا ذلك الثواب ، وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A high garden may be elevated physically or in rank, honor, and distinction.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد هو العلو في المكان ، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد هو العلو في الدرجة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: For the physical interpretation, the garden has ranks above one another, each like the distance between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : الدرجة مثل ما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read with second-person tāʾ and accusative lighiyatan, addressing the Prophet or any listener, or making the faces the subject; 76:20 and 76:19 provide parallels.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي بالتاء على الخطاب لاغية بالنصب

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reads with feminine tāʾ and nominative lighiya.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع بالتاء المنقوطة من فوق مرفوعة على التأنيث لاغية بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read with masculine passive yāʾ and nominative lighiya; masculine agreement is allowed when a feminine subject follows an intervening phrase, or because lighiya denotes laghw.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو لا يسمع بالياء المنقوطة من تحت مضمومة على التذكير لاغية بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One linguistic account treats lighiya and laghw as equivalent, supported by 19:62.
rows.anchor: أنه يقال : لغا يلغو لغوا ولاغية ، فاللاغية واللغو شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second linguistic account makes it an adjective meaning a vain word.
rows.anchor: أن يكون صفة والمعنى لا يسمع كلمة لاغية

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reads it as a word containing vain speech, using faris and daris for a person with a horse or armor as analogies.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش : لاغية أي كلمة ذات لغو كما تقول : فارس ودارس

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal’s account is best: Paradise is a noble gathering of God’s neighbors, purified of idle and false speech, as greater dignity brings greater freedom from it.
rows.anchor: وأحسن الوجوه ما قرره القفال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says its inhabitants speak only wisdom and praise God for lasting blessings.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج لا يتكلم أهل الجنة إلا بالحكمة / والثناء على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as no lies, slander, disbelief in God, or insults.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس يريد لا تسمع فيها كذبا ولا بهتانا ولا كفرا بالله ولا شتما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says people do not swear oaths to one another over drink, as worldly wine drinkers do.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : لا يسمع بعضهم من بعض الحلف عند شراب

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Judge says all useless speech is excluded, especially anything that hurts its hearer.
rows.anchor: اللغو ما لا فائدة فيه ، فالله تعالى نفى عنهم ذلك ويندرج فيه ما يؤذي سامعه

none: The segment contains only the verse-heading transition to 88:12.

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the singular spring as a generic for springs of great abundance, comparing it with 81:14.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : يريد عيونا في غاية الكثرة

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal describes a drink spring flowing across the ground without a channel and running wherever its people wish.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : فيها عين شراب جارية على وجه الأرض في غير أخدود

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says he does not know whether the spring is water or another substance.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : لا أدري بماء أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised couches are high in the air so a believer can see all the blessings and dominion God has granted in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي عالية في الهواء وذلك لأجل أن يرى المؤمن إذا جلس عليها جميع ما أعطاه ربه

rows.speaker: خارجة بن مصعب
rows.claim: Kharija reports that couches are stacked, lower for a friend of God to sit, then rise to the desired height; al-Razi prefers the simpler high-couch account, though the report could increase joy.
rows.anchor: وقال خارجة بن مصعب : بلغنا أنها بعضها فوق بعض فيرتفع ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes couches with gold boards encrusted with beryl, pearls, and rubies, raised in the sky.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هي سرر ألواحها من ذهب مكللة بالزبرجد والدر والياقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cups are handleless drinking vessels; Qatada says they are smaller than pitchers.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأكواب موضوعة }لأكواب الكيزان التي لا عرى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placed means prepared for their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أنها معدة لأهلها كالرجل يلتمس من الرجل شيئا فيقول هو ههنا موضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placed can mean set beside flowing springs and filled whenever people want a drink.
rows.anchor: موضوعة على حافاة العيون الجارية كلما أرادوا الشرب وجدوها مملوءة من الشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean arranged before them as beautiful vessels of gold, silver, or gems, enjoyed with their drink.
rows.anchor: موضوعة بين أيديهم لاستحسانهم إياها بسبب كونها من ذهب أو فضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their size is moderate rather than too large or too small, in line with the phrasing qaddarūhā taqdīra.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد موضوعة عن حد الكبر أي هي أوساط بين الصغر والكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namarīq are cushions, according to all commentators; al-Farra also heard the singular pronounced with kasra from Arabs.
rows.anchor: النمارق هي الوسائد في قول الجميع واحدها نمرقة بضم النون ، وزاد الفراء سماعا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the cushions are arranged side by side so a person may sit on one and lean against another.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : وسائد مصفوفة بعضها إلى جانب بعض أينما أراد أن يجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarābī are rugs or thick carpets; the language experts agree on this meaning and give the singular forms zarbiya and zarbiy.
rows.anchor: يعني البسط والطنافس واحدها زربية وزربي بكسر الزاي في قول جميع أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mabthūtha means spread out or distributed around the gathering places.
rows.anchor: وتفسير مبثوثة مبسوطة منشورة أو مفرقة في المجالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel, sky, mountains, and earth support resurrection by proving a wise Creator: specified forms require a capable particularizer, design establishes knowledge, and a self-sufficient Creator is wise.
rows.anchor: لأن الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية فاختصاص كل واحد منها بالوصف الذي لأجله امتاز على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human interdependence requires organized society and moral obligations with promise and warning, which entail resurrection, Paradise, and Hell.
rows.anchor: وذلك الانتظام لا يحسن إلا مع التكليف المشتمل على الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures furnish the same proof, so varied, unrelated examples signal that no type is exempt; every high or low, small or great, beautiful or ugly body points to God, as 17:44 says.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن هذا الوجه من الاستدلال غير مختص بنوع دون نوع بل هو عام في الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second approach is to detail the benefits and special properties of each example, then explain how the examples correspond.
rows.anchor: نبين ما في كل واحد من هذه الأشياء من المنافع والخواص الدالة على الحاجة إلى الصانع المدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels uniquely serve as meat, milk, mounts, freight carriers, and adornment; 36:71–72 and 16:5–7 describe these benefits, which other animals do not combine.
rows.anchor: فتارة يقتني ليؤكل لحمه وتارة ليشرب لبنه وتارة ليحمل الإنسان في الأسفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For each use the camel outperforms animals specialized for only one: it yields abundant milk and meat, travels far on little fodder despite thirst, and carries heavy loads.
rows.anchor: أنها إن جعلت حلوبة سقت فأروت الكثير ، وإن جعلت أكولة أطعمت وأشبعت الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels mattered deeply to Arabs: they paid blood compensation in camels, rulers gave poets a hundred, and camels were beautiful to watch, as 16:6 notes.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الحيوان كان أعظم الحيوانات وقعا في قلب العرب ولذلك فإنهم جعلوا دية قتل الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi recounts losing the way with companions in a desert; a camel found the route by retaining a winding path that rational people could not retrace.
rows.anchor: ضللنا الطريق فقدموا جملا وتبعوه فكان ذلك الجمل ينعطف من تل إلى تل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite great strength, the camel submits to a small child and kneels for loading before rising with its burden.
rows.anchor: مع كونها في غاية القوة على العمل مباينة لغيرها في الانقياد والطاعة لأضعف الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs know camels intimately, so directing them to contemplate the animal’s remarkable construction is especially apt.
rows.anchor: إن العرب من أعرف الناس بأحوال الإبل في صحتها وسقمها ومنافعها ومضارها

none: Verse heading only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is raised to a great height without support or pillars.
rows.anchor: رفعا بعيد المدى بلا إمساك وبغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are set firmly in place and neither lean nor move.
rows.anchor: نصبا ثابتا فهي راسخة لا تميل ولا تزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is leveled and prepared as a habitation; its apparent flatness does not disprove a spherical earth because a vast globe looks locally flat.
rows.anchor: سطحا بتمهيد وتوطئة ، فهي مهاد للمتقلب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference that the earth is not spherical is weak: on a sufficiently immense sphere, each region appears flat.
rows.anchor: ومن / الناس من استدل بهذا على أن الأرض ليست بكرة وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reads the four verbs as active first-person forms, with the object omitted: I created, raised, set up, and spread them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي عليه السلام كيف خلقت ورفعت ونصبت وسطحت على البناء للفاعل وتاء الضمير

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Some take camels as clouds by analogy with camel imagery in poetry; al-Zamakhshari says this is a metaphor, not a lexical name for clouds, making the sequence coherent.
rows.anchor: إنما رأى السحاب مشبها بالإبل في كثير من أشعارهم ، فجوز أن يراد بها السحاب على طريق التشبيه والمجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literally read, the examples suit Arab travelers crossing barren land by camel: solitude invites thought, and they see the camel, sky, mountains, and earth in turn.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يسافرون كثيرا ، لأن بلدتهم بلدة خالية من الزرع ، وكانت أسفارهم في أكثر الأمر على الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence directs people to reflect in solitude, when pride or envy will not obstruct thought and the four surrounding sights occupy their attention.
rows.anchor: أمره بالنظر وقت الخلوة والانفراد عن الغير حتى لا تحمله داعية الكبر والحسد على ترك النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another link divides created things into those that combine wisdom with an appeal to desire and those whose construction displays wisdom without such an appeal.
rows.anchor: منها ما يكون للحكمة وللشهوة فيها نصيب معا ، ومنها ما يكون للحكمة فيها نصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful people, gardens, gold, and silver carry worldly desire that can overpower reflection, so God does not direct people to reason through them.
rows.anchor: فلم يأمر تعالى بالنظر فيها ، لأنه لم يؤمن عند النظر إليها وفيها أن تصير داعية الشهوة غالبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels, sky, mountains, and earth display wisdom without feeding desire; this lets contemplation proceed clearly, which is why God commands it.
rows.anchor: لما كان هذا القسم بحيث يكمل نصيب الحكمة فيه مع الأمن من زحمة الشهوة لا جرم أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving divine oneness and resurrection, God commands reminder through such proofs, reflection on them, and warning against neglect; the Messenger must also endure obstacles and is commissioned for this task.
rows.anchor: وتذكير الرسول إنما يكون بذكر هذه الأدلة وأمثالها والبعث على النظر فيها

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses musayṭir as one with power or control, like the descriptions in 50:45 and 10:99.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { * بمصيطر } بمسلط ، كقوله : { يقولون وما أنت عليهم بجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Tamim’s dialect the tāʾ is open because their verb sayṭara is transitive.
rows.anchor: هو في لغة تميم مفتوح الطاء على أن سيطر متعد عندهم

rows.speaker: all exegetes
rows.claim: The Messenger’s role is reminder, not compulsion to faith or power to kill; commentators say the verse was later abrogated by the fighting verse.
rows.anchor: فأما أن تكون مسلطا عليهم حتى تقتلهم ، أو تكرههم على الإيمان فلا ، قالوا : ثم نسختها آية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One connected exception attaches to the command to remind: remind, except those who turn away and disbelieve.
rows.anchor: التقدير : فذكر إلا من تولى وكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connected exception attaches to not being a controller: the Prophet is not master over them except those who turn away; the objection that fighting was not yet commanded receives a qualified answer.
rows.anchor: أنه استثناء عن الضمير في { سواء عليهم } ( الغاشية : 22 ) والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disconnected exception means the Prophet is not accountable for them, but God punishes those who turn away; the construction permits an added anna, unlike a connected exception.
rows.anchor: لست بمسئول عليهم ، لكن من تولى منهم فإن الله يعذبه العذاب الأكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has alif-lāmā for attention; Ibn Masud reads fa-innahu yuʿadhdhibuhu.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( ألا من تولى ) على التنبيه ، وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( فإنه يعذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest punishment is disbelief’s punishment, greater than punishment for sin, as 32:21 contrasts the nearer and greater punishments.
rows.anchor: أنه قد بلغ حد عذاب الكفر وهو الأكبر ، لأن ما عداه من عذاب الفسق دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that it means punishment in Hell’s lowest level.
rows.anchor: هو العذاب في الدرك الأسفل في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading places the greatest punishment in worldly killing, captivity of children, and seizure of property; al-Razi judges the first explanation closer.
rows.anchor: قد / يكون العذاب الأكبر حاصلا في الدنيا ، وذلك بالقتل وسبي الذرية وغنيمة الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return statement extends the previous threat and consoles the Prophet: despite their rejection, the disbelievers return to God’s promised judgment.
rows.anchor: وإن عاندوا وكذبوا وجحدوا فإن مرجعهم إلى الموعد الذي وعدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God is not obliged to collect His own right, accounting is required by His unbreakable promise or by wisdom, lest failure to punish oppressors imply approval of injustice.
rows.anchor: ذلك واجب عليه إما بحكم الوعد الذي يمتنع وقوع الخلف فيه ، وإما في الحكمة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المدني
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads īyābahum with a doubled yāʾ; al-Zamakhshari derives it either as a verbal noun of ayb or through awb and a sequence of sound changes.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر المدني : { إيابهم } بالتشديد . قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وجهه أن يكون فيعالا مصدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the return phrase intensifies the warning because their return is solely to the Almighty, who can exact retribution.
rows.anchor: فائدة تقديم الظرف التشديد بالوعيد ، فإن { إيابهم } ليس إلا إلى الجبار المقتدر على الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God must account for them, and He reckons even the smallest things.
rows.anchor: وأن حسابهم ليس بواجب إلا عليه ، وهو الذي يحاسب على النقير والقطمير
